clue.text: see 14ac.
Red-nose star puts convenience before specialities

blocks.note: a public convenience is a lavatory, and WC (water closet) is the usual abbreviation
one's fields are one's areas of expertise

explanation.surface: A comedian with a red nose puts a toilet ahead of his particular talents.
explanation.walkthrough: W.C. Fields, the American film comic, was famous for his bulbous drinker's nose.
explanation.definitionFit: The comic actor W.C. Fields was known for his heavy drinking and his famously red, bulbous nose.

clue.text: see 14ac.
Be an egg and have sex!

blocks.note: first meaning: what happens to an egg when a hen produces it
second meaning: the slang phrase for having intercourse

explanation.surface: A cheeky exhortation to be an egg and have sex, as if both were the same thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen's egg is said to be laid, and the slang phrase for scoring sexually uses the same two words.

clue.text: Get attached, as not often screwed

indicators.note: something screwed is twisted out of its proper shape, so the letters before it are twisted into new order

blocks.note: the letters of these three words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A rueful remark that people seldom get sexually involved, with a double meaning on screwed.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten onto something is to latch on or cling to it, a phrasal synonym for becoming attached.

clue.text: L&G involved with Frau Merkel's approach to economics?

definitions.note: a description of a careful, thrifty policy; the answer is the adjective for it

indicators.note: things involved are tangled up together, so the letters get mixed into a new order

blocks.note: the two letters, ignoring the ampersand
taken as written; Frau is German for Mrs

explanation.surface: Legal & General, the insurer, gets caught up with the German chancellor's austerity.
explanation.walkthrough: Angela Merkel was known for insisting on budget discipline across the eurozone; L&G is the insurance firm Legal & General.
explanation.definitionFit: Merkel's economic policy was famously thrifty and sparing with spending, which is exactly what being frugal means.

clue.text: London Eye? Move like a queen, tart!

definitions.note: the question mark flags cockney rhyming slang: the answer is the slang term for an eye

blocks.note: to mince is to walk with affected dainty steps, a stereotype of a camp gay man (queen)
a tart is a kind of pie

explanation.surface: Someone sashays past the London Eye wheel and is hailed as a tart.
explanation.walkthrough: In cockney rhyming slang a phrase stands for the word it rhymes with, so the answer means eye in London speech; the big wheel is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang uses the festive pastry's name as a substitute for eye, so a London eye is exactly this.

clue.text: Fair pissed with Bill's great mass

indicators.note: pissed is slang for drunk, and drunk letters stagger out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written
a bill is an account, abbreviated AC

explanation.surface: A fair-haired drinker named Bill is very fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill's great mass' reads like a fat man's bulk; the 's is just 'is' linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The continent is an enormous landmass, the second largest on Earth, so it is a fair description.

clue.text: Maybe Albert would get Cameron's party put in order

blocks.note: David Cameron led the Conservatives, abbreviated CON
to sort is to arrange in order

explanation.surface: A puzzle over whether Albert would see the Tory party tidied up.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Albert was husband of Queen Victoria; 'Maybe' signals he is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Albert was Queen Victoria's husband, and the spouse of a reigning monarch is called by this title.

clue.text: Mole, one with something due shortly by editor?

indicators.note: shortly says the phrase before it is cut down to its usual abbreviated form

blocks.note: one as the article a
a debit is something owed, and accountants write it Dr
Ian Hislop is the long-serving editor of Private Eye, where this puzzle appeared

explanation.surface: A mole has something owed to it soon, courtesy of an editor.
explanation.walkthrough: Adrian Mole is Sue Townsend's comic teenage diarist; the editor is Private Eye's own Ian Hislop.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional diarist Adrian Mole, created by Sue Townsend, is the famous bearer of this surname, so the forename fits it.

clue.text: Turned on by giant nuts, getting engaged in suit

definitions.note: describes the person; the answer is a noun, one engaged in a lawsuit

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the word it follows goes mad and rearranges

blocks.note: a lamp turned on is lit
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone aroused by a huge man's testicles ends up in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A party to a lawsuit, either suing or being sued, is someone involved in legal proceedings over a claim.

clue.text: Fickle celebrity on right deserts – gleefully anticipated by Ukip?

definitions.note: a description of the event; the answer is the noun for it

indicators.note: deserts means abandons, so the letter named just before it walks out and is dropped
fickle means changeable, so the remaining letters change their positions

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A fickle right-wing star walks out, and Ukip rubs its hands.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove R from celebrity on, then rearrange. Ukip, the UK Independence Party, gained big boosts in by-elections caused by defecting MPs.
explanation.definitionFit: A by-election is a single-seat poll held between general elections, which insurgent parties like Ukip relished as chances to win.

clue.text: Having illicit sex and not pulling out

blocks.note: first meaning: conducting an affair
second meaning: continuing rather than withdrawing

explanation.surface: A smutty description of an affair conducted without withdrawal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to have a clandestine affair and to continue or persist instead of stopping or withdrawing.

clue.text: (& 1dn./3dn.) Take a benevolent view of Ukip, OK? Only 2/3rds of London is done for

indicators.note: two thirds of a six-letter word keeps only four letters and drops the final third
something done for is wrecked, so the letters before it are broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plea to think well of Ukip, since London is largely a lost cause for them.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep the first four of London's six letters (LOND), then rearrange them with Ukip, OK and Only.
explanation.definitionFit: To look kindly upon something is to regard it with favour and goodwill, an idiom for viewing it benevolently.

clue.text: "Scrubber": Times on Brenda

blocks.note: eras are periods of time
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for Queen Elizabeth II, whose royal cipher is ER

explanation.surface: The Times newspaper calls the Queen a scrubber, a vulgar insult.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' places one piece after the other; scrubber is British slang for a promiscuous woman, but here it is a rubber.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber used to remove pencil marks scrubs them off the page, so it is literally a scrubber.

clue.text: Alec's changed into skirt – get back!

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the name's letters are altered in order
going into something means being placed inside it

blocks.note: the name, taken as written
a skirt is an edging or border, a rim

explanation.surface: Alec has put on a skirt, and someone wants it returned.
explanation.walkthrough: Skirt as a noun is the lower edge of something, hence a rim.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclaim something is to recover or retrieve it, take possession of it once more.

clue.text: Clegg not quite finished yet? Sadly that's a rather fine point

indicators.note: not quite finished means stopping just short, so the last letter is lopped off
sadly means badly or poorly, so the word before it comes out wrongly ordered

blocks.note: Nick Clegg was Liberal Democrat leader and deputy prime minister
the letters of yet, rearranged

explanation.surface: A jibe that Nick Clegg's career isn't quite over yet, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick Clegg, Lib Dem leader in the 2010 coalition, loses his last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A nicety is a subtle distinction or small detail, a delicate point of precision.

clue.text: On the lookout for sex and having a good time in the main?

definitions.text: having a good time in the main?

blocks.note: first meaning: looking for a casual sexual partner

blocks.clueFragment: having a good time in the main?
blocks.note: second meaning: enjoying a holiday at sea, the main being the ocean

explanation.surface: Someone prowling for sex who, on the whole, is enjoying themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' looks like 'mostly' but is the main, the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for seeking casual sex and also describes holidaying on an ocean liner sailing the seas.

clue.text: Condition of large corporation?

blocks.note: surface reading: the state of health of a big company
setter's reading: corporation is an old jokey word for a pot belly, so this is the medical condition of being fat

explanation.surface: A business report asking how a big company is faring.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporation is dated humorous slang for a paunch, which turns the business question into a medical one.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a large paunch is the defining sign of being seriously overweight, the medical condition named here.

clue.text: (& 25ac.) Salmond's first to bear outcome – it's part of the healing process

blocks.note: the opening letter of the name
to cart is to carry or bear

explanation.surface: Alex Salmond must accept the result of the Scottish vote and heal the wounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Alex Salmond led the Scottish National Party through the 2014 independence referendum.
explanation.definitionFit: Fibrous tissue forms over a wound as it closes, so it is a visible stage of the body mending itself.

clue.text: Stand for election (rather boring) and reach the end of the booze

blocks.note: to run is to stand as a candidate
dry means dull or uninteresting

clue.text: Boris-style riposte? "Rollicking saucy books!"

blocks.note: the letters of both words, taken as written

clue.text: Desires no end to Tory's income

the final letter of the word

clue.text: see 20ac.
Sort of politician Blair became: "Right" rather than "New"

explanation.walkthrough: Swap the N in Blair's first name for an R; the dig is that New Labour drifted right.
